quiz.question: How many bits are in an IPv6 address, and how many hexadecimal hextets are used to represent it?
options: 64 bits arranged in 4 groups of 16 bits
128 bits arranged in 8 groups of 16 bits (hextets)
256 bits arranged in 16 groups of 16 bits
32 bits arranged in 4 decimal octets

quiz.question: Which of the following is the correctly shortened canonical representation of 2001:0db8:0000:0000:0000:0000:0000:0042?
Which IPv6 address range is designated for non-routable Link-Local communication on a local wire segment?
options: fc00::/7 (Unique-Local)

quiz.question: Why is /64 considered the standard, mandatory subnet size for most conventional IPv6 LANs?
options: Because IPv6 routers cannot route any prefix longer than /64.
Because Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC) requires a 64-bit Interface Identifier (IID) to configure addresses automatically.
To match the standard 64-byte minimum Ethernet frame size.
Because /64 provides exactly 254 usable host addresses.

quiz.question: What protocol replaces IPv4 ARP for link-layer MAC address resolution in IPv6 networks?
options: Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP), utilizing ICMPv6 Neighbor Solicitation (NS) and Neighbor Advertisement (NA) messages
DHCPv6 Address Resolution Agent
Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP)
NAT64 Protocol Translation

quiz.question: In Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC), how does a client host learn its default gateway?
options: From the DHCPv6 Server Option 3 default router field.
From the source link-local IPv6 address of the router that transmitted the Router Advertisement (RA).
By querying the local DNS server for a gateway SRV record.
By picking the first usable address in the /64 prefix (e.g. ::1).

quiz.question: What is the difference between Stateless DHCPv6 and Stateful DHCPv6?
options: Stateless DHCPv6 assigns IP addresses; Stateful DHCPv6 only provides DNS.
Stateless DHCPv6 lets hosts form their own IP via SLAAC while providing additional parameters (such as DNS servers); Stateful DHCPv6 leases managed IPv6 addresses and tracks client state.
Stateless DHCPv6 requires a router; Stateful DHCPv6 operates without routers.
Stateless DHCPv6 is used exclusively for IPv4 translation.

quiz.question: What does the 'Happy Eyeballs' algorithm (RFC 8305) accomplish in dual-stack client applications?
options: It compresses 128-bit IPv6 addresses into 32-bit hashes.
It attempts parallel connections to IPv6 and IPv4 destinations, favoring IPv6 but rapidly falling back to IPv4 within ~250ms if IPv6 connectivity is broken or impaired.
It encrypts DNS AAAA queries using TLS 1.3.
It automatically translates IPv4 private addresses into IPv6 link-local addresses.

quiz.question: How do NAT64 and DNS64 cooperate to allow IPv6-only clients to access legacy IPv4-only web servers?
options: DNS64 translates the client's MAC address; NAT64 converts TCP to UDP.

DNS64 synthesizes a synthetic IPv6 AAAA record (using prefix 64:ff9b::/96 + the IPv4 hex) for IPv4-only domains; the client sends packets to this synthetic IPv6 address, which the NAT64 gateway translates into real IPv4 packets.
NAT64 replaces the operating system kernel with an IPv4 emulator.
DNS64 tunnels the IPv4 traffic inside an SSH tunnel.

quiz.question: Why is RA Guard (Router Advertisement Guard) recommended on enterprise Layer 2 access switches?
options: To block all ICMPv6 traffic from entering the network.
To drop unauthorized or rogue Router Advertisements on access edge ports, preventing rogue devices from hijacking the default gateway or advertising bogus prefixes.
To accelerate Spanning Tree Protocol convergence.
To compress IPv6 headers before transmission over Wi-Fi.

theorySections.title: Why IPv6 is Necessary: The Mathematics of Address Exhaustion
paragraphs: IPv4 provides a 32-bit address space yielding 4,294,967,296 addresses ($2^{32}$). With billions of smartphones, IoT sensors, cloud virtual machines, and containers, the global pool administered by IANA and regional internet registries (ARIN, RIPE, APNIC) was officially exhausted.

IPv6 does not automatically make web applications faster. Latency depends on BGP routing paths, fiber distance, and peering agreements. Because the base IPv6 header is 40 bytes (compared to 20 bytes in IPv4), small payloads carry slightly higher protocol overhead.

theorySections.title: IPv6 Address Notation, Hexadecimal Groups & Compression Rules
paragraphs: An IPv6 address is written as eight 16-bit hexadecimal groups (hextets) separated by colons: 2001:0db8:0001:0000:0000:0000:0000:0025
Leading zeros in any 16-bit hextet can be dropped: • 0db8 → db8 • 0001 → 1 • 0000 → 0 • 0025 → 25 Trailing or middle zeros must NEVER be dropped (1020 is NOT 12).

A single contiguous sequence of all-zero hextets can be replaced with a double colon (::): • 2001:db8:1:0:0:0:0:25 → 2001:db8:1::25 Critical constraint: :: can be used only once per address. Using it twice makes the omitted zero count ambiguous!

theorySections.title: IPv6 Address Types, Scopes & Special Prefixes
paragraphs: IPv6 categorizes addresses by scope (link-local, unique-local, global) and transmission type (unicast, multicast, anycast).

theorySections.title: IPv6 Prefixes, Hierarchical Subnetting & The Sacred /64 Rule
paragraphs: Subnetting in IPv6 is radically simpler than IPv4. Because address space is abundant, engineers never subnet to conserve individual host IPs. Instead, every standard LAN subnet is assigned a /64 prefix.

Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (SLAAC) requires a /64 prefix to operate. Even if an office VLAN has only 5 printers, assigning a /64 preserves routing standardization and ensures feature compatibility across all operating systems.

theorySections.title: Neighbor Discovery Protocol (NDP — RFC 4861) & ICMPv6
paragraphs: IPv6 eliminates Layer 2 ARP broadcasts in favor of NDP, built on ICMPv6. NDP handles address resolution, router discovery, prefix discovery, duplicate address detection, and next-hop reachability.

Instead of broadcasting to all devices, an NS is addressed to ff02::1:ffxx:xxxx (formed by appending the target's last 24 bits to ff02::1:ff00:0/104). The switch hashes this to Ethernet multicast MAC 33:33:ff:xx:xx:xx, ensuring only the intended host's NIC silicon wakes up to inspect the frame!

theorySections.title: SLAAC: Stateless Address Autoconfiguration (RFC 4862)
paragraphs: SLAAC enables true plug-and-play network attachment without a DHCP server. The host learns the /64 network prefix from the local router's RA and generates its own 64-bit Interface Identifier (IID).

theorySections.title: DHCPv6: Stateless vs. Stateful Operating Modes
paragraphs: DHCPv6 operates in two distinct modes governed by the Managed (M) and Other (O) flag bits in the router's Router Advertisement.

Hosts form their own IPv6 addresses via SLAAC. They send an Information-Request to DHCPv6 solely to receive auxiliary configuration (DNS servers, domain search lists). Server maintains zero lease state.
The DHCPv6 server leases centrally managed IPv6 addresses and tracks leases in a database, mimicking IPv4 DHCP. Used in high-compliance enterprises requiring strict IP auditing.
DHCPv6 does NOT provide the default gateway address! Unlike IPv4 DHCP Option 3, an IPv6 host ALWAYS learns its default router from ICMPv6 Router Advertisements.

theorySections.title: Dual-Stack Networking & Happy Eyeballs (RFC 8305)
paragraphs: In dual-stack networks, devices run IPv4 and IPv6 concurrently on the same interface. When resolving a domain, DNS returns both an A record (IPv4) and a AAAA record (IPv6).

Modern web browsers race connection attempts: they initiate a TCP SYN over IPv6, wait a brief 250ms fallback timer, and if IPv6 has not connected, start a parallel IPv4 connection. Whichever completes first wins the race, eliminating connection hangs!
